subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Small molecule targeted therapy: kinase inhibitors, synthetic lethality, resistance mechanisms and bypass pathways

steps.tx: First-generation reversible EGFR **tyrosine kinase inhibitors** erlotinib and gefitinib competitively bind the intracellular ATP-binding pocket of EGFR. These agents demonstrate marked efficacy against classical activating EGFR mutations, specifically **exon 19 deletion** and the exon 21 L858R point substitution in non-small cell lung cancer. Suppressing downstream MAPK and PI3K/Akt survival signalling cascades induces profound tumour regression in oncogene-addicted adenocarcinomas.

rows: Irreversible mutant-selective covalent inhibition sparing wild-type

steps.tx: Third-generation irreversible mutant-selective TKI **Osimertinib** forms a stable covalent bond with cysteine-797 within the ATP-binding cleft. Osimertinib selectively overcomes the secondary T790M resistance **gatekeeper mutation** while demonstrating negligible binding affinity against wild-type EGFR, substantially minimizing cutaneous and gastrointestinal adverse effects. Furthermore, osimertinib penetrates the blood-brain barrier effectively, providing excellent intracranial disease control in advanced NSCLC.

steps.tx: In oncogene-addicted **ALK-rearranged** lung cancer, second-generation ALK inhibitors **alectinib** and brigatinib deliver dramatic clinical superiority over first-generation crizotinib. In the landmark ALEX trial, alectinib demonstrated superior progression-free survival and profoundly reduced central nervous system progression. Alectinib exhibits potent systemic potency against common crizotinib-resistant secondary ALK mutations and achieves high cerebrospinal fluid concentrations without requiring efflux transporter evasion.

right.title: Crizotinib
points: High rate of central nervous system recurrence
Replaced by next-generation inhibitors in front-line

steps.tx: Constitutively active **BRAF V600E** kinase mutations drive uncontrolled proliferative signalling in metastatic melanoma, colorectal, and thyroid cancers. Administering combination therapy with BRAF inhibitor dabrafenib and MEK inhibitor trametinib achieves rapid tumour shrinkage while suppressing paradoxical **MAPK reactivation**. Concurrent MEK blockade prevents RAF dimerisation in BRAF wild-type keratinocytes, dramatically lowering the incidence of secondary cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas.

steps.tx: Targeted **PARP inhibitors** olaparib, rucaparib, and talazoparib selectively kill tumour cells deficient in homologous recombination DNA repair through **synthetic lethality**. PARP inhibitors trap PARP1 and PARP2 enzymes on damaged DNA single-strand breaks, stalling replication forks that collapse into double-strand breaks. In BRCA1 or BRCA2 deficient cells unable to repair double-strand breaks via homologous recombination, catastrophic genomic instability triggers rapid apoptosis.

steps.tx: Oral **CDK4/6 inhibitors** palbociclib, ribociclib, and abemaciclib block cyclin D-dependent phosphorylation of retinoblastoma protein RB1. Blocking RB1 phosphorylation prevents release of E2F transcription factors, enforcing cell cycle arrest at the restriction checkpoint in **G1 phase**. Combining CDK4/6 inhibitors with endocrine therapy doubles progression-free survival in advanced estrogen receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.

steps.tx: Small molecule **VEGFR TKIs** lenvatinib, cabozantinib, and sorafenib disrupt pathological tumour **angiogenesis** by blocking vascular endothelial growth factor receptor phosphorylation. In addition to VEGFR1, VEGFR2, and VEGFR3, these multikinase agents inhibit RET, MET, KIT, and FGFR receptors, starving solid tumours of oxygen and nutrients. Common class-related toxicities include systemic hypertension, hand-foot skin reaction, proteinuria, and fatigue.

rows: Renal cell carcinoma and hepatocellular carcinoma

steps.tx: Secondary **TKI resistance** inexorably evolves through on-target secondary point mutations or activation of parallel compensatory signalling cascades. Common biological resistance mechanisms include target gene amplification, emergent gatekeeper variants, and **bypass pathway** signalling such as MET amplification, HER2 amplification, or histologic transformation to small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma. Overcoming resistance requires repeat tissue or liquid biopsy genomic profiling to direct next-line salvage therapies.
